provider.description: Hosted OAuth provider. Pollar owns the app registration.

redirect_uri.description: Where the bridge delivers the single-use code, as `?code=…&state=…`. Must be registered for this consumer in POLLAR_REDIRECT_URI_WHITELIST. Omit it to use the poll flow (GET /v1/pollar/oauth/sessions/{state}), which is the right shape for a wallet that cannot be addressed by URL.

code_challenge.description: PKCE challenge (RFC 7636): BASE64URL(SHA256(code_verifier)). Optional, but once supplied the matching `code_verifier` is required to redeem. Bind the code to the wallet that asked for it — a code that leaks out of a browser or a log is then useless on its own.

code_challenge_method.description: S256 only. `plain` offers no protection across a redirect.

dpop_jwk.description: The wallet's DPoP public key. When present, Pollar binds the minted tokens to it and only the wallet can use or refresh them.

device_label.description: Label shown in Pollar's session list, so a user can tell this device apart from their others when revoking.

state.description: Opaque handle for this handshake. Echoed back on the redirect and used to poll. Correlate on it — the bridge issues no other identifier.

authorization_url.description: Send the user here. It is Pollar's hosted OAuth entry point with the api_key, client_session_id and the bridge's own callback already assembled — the wallet opens it and touches nothing else.

redirect_uri.description: Where the code will be delivered, or null when this handshake is in poll mode and the wallet must read it back from the bridge.

expires_at.description: When the handshake stops being redeemable. The user has until then to finish the consent screen.

status.description: `pending` — waiting for the user. `authorized` — the code is in this response. `exchanging` — a redemption is in flight. `consumed` — done. `failed` / `expired` — terminal, start a new handshake.

code.description: The single-use bridge code, present only while the status is `authorized` and only until it expires. Redeem it at POST /v1/pollar/oauth/token.

code_expires_at.description: When the code stops being redeemable.

error_code.description: Pollar's own error code when the handshake ended badly.

code.description: The `code` the bridge delivered to the redirect URI, or returned by the poll route.

code_verifier.description: PKCE verifier (RFC 7636). Required when the handshake was opened with a `code_challenge`, refused when it was not.

type.description: `internal` is the virtual wallet Pollar custodies in its KMS — the one a social login gets. `smart` is a passkey C-address, `external` a wallet the user connected themselves.

address.description: Stellar public key (`G…`), or the C-address for a smart wallet.

exists_on_stellar.description: False when the account has no XLM reserve yet — the Deferred funding mode. Activate it with POST /v1/pollar/wallets/activate once your own business event says the user has earned an on-chain account.

refresh_token.description: Single-use refresh token. Pollar rotates it on every refresh and treats a replay as a compromise, revoking the family.

token_type.description: `DPoP` when the handshake supplied a `dpop_jwk`: every call must then carry a proof signed by the wallet's private key, and this service can no longer refresh or revoke on its behalf.

expires_at.description: Access-token expiry, epoch milliseconds as Pollar reports it.

user_id.description: Pollar's id for the end user.

wallet.description: The wallet the session acts as. Null address means Pollar has not provisioned one yet.

wallets.description: Every wallet linked to the user, including the one above.

publishable_key.description: The Pollar publishable key for this network. The wallet needs it in `x-pollar-api-key` on every direct call, and it is public by design.

api_base_url.description: Base URL the access token is good against, version included. Call it directly; this service does not proxy the wallet surface.

refresh_token.description: The `refresh_token` from a previous exchange or refresh. Single-use: Pollar rotates it and rejects a reuse of the old one.

access_token.description: The access token of the session to revoke.

everywhere.description: Revoke every device, not just this one.

public_key.description: The wallet's Stellar public key, as the session reported it.
